definition: To add something to the end of a document or text
example_sentence: The full data set is appended to the report.

definition: To make a process work by machine instead of by people
example_sentence: Many banks have automated their customer services.

definition: A product that can be bought and sold, especially raw materials
example_sentence: Oil is the world's most traded commodity.

definition: To behave according to accepted rules or standards
example_sentence: Teenagers often feel pressure to conform to their friends.

definition: To be a sign of something, or to mean something
example_sentence: In the chart, red dots denote cities with high pollution.

definition: To force people to leave their homes, or to take the place of something
example_sentence: The war displaced millions of people.

definition: To balance one effect with an opposite one
example_sentence: Higher prices were offset by rising wages.

definition: A person who works in a profession, especially medicine or law
example_sentence: Medical practitioners must renew their licenses every five years.

definition: The possibility that something will happen
example_sentence: The prospect of peace seems distant.

definition: Very new and different, or believing in extreme change
example_sentence: The report calls for radical changes to the tax system.

definition: To end something, especially officially
example_sentence: The company terminated the contract without warning.

definition: To leave someone or something permanently, or to stop doing something
example_sentence: The project was abandoned because of rising costs.

definition: A feeling of worry or conflict, or the state of being stretched tight
example_sentence: Tension between the two countries is rising.

definition: To tell someone that something is true so they do not worry
example_sentence: The minister assured the public that the water was safe.

definition: To stop happening or existing
example_sentence: The factory ceased production last year.

definition: To happen at the same time, or to agree with something
example_sentence: The rise in crime coincided with the economic crisis.

definition: To begin, especially officially
example_sentence: Construction will commence in the spring.

definition: The length of time that something lasts
example_sentence: The duration of the study was three years.

definition: To gradually damage or destroy something
example_sentence: Rising prices have eroded the value of wages.

definition: Between two levels or stages
example_sentence: The course is designed for intermediate students.

definition: To try to help two sides reach an agreement
example_sentence: A neutral country offered to mediate between the two sides.

definition: The amount by which two things cover the same area or share features
example_sentence: There is a large overlap between the two studies.

definition: A part of something larger
example_sentence: A large portion of the budget goes to health care.

definition: A set of rules for how something must be done
example_sentence: Doctors followed a strict protocol during the trial.

definition: To stop someone from doing something, or to control something
example_sentence: The government tried to restrain rising prices.

definition: A description of what could happen in the future
example_sentence: In the worst scenario, sea levels could rise by a meter.

definition: An area of activity or interest, or a round solid shape
example_sentence: Women are gaining influence in the political sphere.

definition: Lower in rank or less important
example_sentence: Personal interests should be subordinate to the public good.

definition: To stop something for a time, or to hang something
example_sentence: The school suspended classes during the storm.

definition: To bring together into a single whole
example_sentence: The new leader promised to unify the country.

definition: To break a law, rule or agreement
example_sentence: The company violated safety rules.

definition: Next to or near something
example_sentence: The hospital is adjacent to the university.

definition: To form an idea or plan in your mind
example_sentence: It is hard to conceive of a world without computers.

definition: About to happen or appear, or willing to give information
example_sentence: The results will appear in a forthcoming article.

definition: To tend to think or behave in a certain way
example_sentence: Most readers incline to agree with the author.

definition: To use a law or principle to support an action or argument
example_sentence: The government invoked emergency powers.

definition: An amount of money that must be paid to the government
example_sentence: A new levy on plastic bags was introduced.

definition: Continuing to exist or develop
example_sentence: The investigation is ongoing.

definition: To create a problem or danger, or to ask a question

definition: Easy to understand or do
example_sentence: The instructions are clear and straightforward.

definition: To experience a process of change or treatment

definition: By which; used to explain how something works
example_sentence: The law created a system whereby workers can report abuse.

definition: To make something stronger or more effective
example_sentence: The new evidence bolsters the theory.

definition: To control or limit something, especially something harmful
example_sentence: New rules aim to curb air pollution.

definition: To consider or judge something in a particular way
example_sentence: The building was deemed unsafe.

definition: To become gradually smaller in size or number
example_sentence: The number of bees continues to dwindle.

definition: To fall very quickly and suddenly
example_sentence: Share prices plummet when investors lose confidence.

definition: To make two ideas or facts agree, or to restore friendly relations
example_sentence: It is hard to reconcile economic growth with environmental protection.

definition: To prevent someone from doing what they plan
example_sentence: Police thwart dozens of attacks every year.

definition: To involve something as a necessary part or result

definition: To put something at risk of being harmed or lost
example_sentence: One mistake could jeopardize the whole project.

definition: To be greater or more important than something else
example_sentence: The benefits of the vaccine far outweigh the risks.

definition: A disadvantage or problem

definition: A problem that delays progress
example_sentence: The failed test was a serious setback for the team.

definition: Of great importance because other things depend on it
example_sentence: Teachers play a pivotal role in children's development.

definition: In a way that is clear and easy to notice
example_sentence: Crime has fallen markedly in recent years.
